about: A decide corpus, not a validate one. policy-guard/1 grades a spend as ALLOW, ESCALATE or DENY. Folded into a boolean, ALLOW and ESCALATE become one answer — and the difference between them is a human being asked before a signature happens, which is the entire point of the profile. So the answer is a verdict from a closed, declared vocabulary, and this corpus asserts which one each spend must draw.

protocol.note: The verdict must be one of the set's declared `outcomes`. A reply outside that vocabulary is UNREADABLE — the program failed to speak the protocol — which is a different finding from answering the wrong verdict.

sets.name: envelopes
sets.about: A spend is ALLOWed under the escalation ceiling, ESCALATEd above it (a human is asked), and DENIED above the per-transaction cap (no human can wave it through).

cases.why: A routine spend far below the ceiling clears without anyone being asked.
The ceiling is the last ALLOW, not the first ESCALATE: escalation is for spends ABOVE it.
One unit over the ceiling asks a human. This is the case the whole profile exists for — a boolean would have called it ALLOW.
A large but not impossible spend escalates; it is not denied, because a human may still approve it.
The cap is the last ESCALATE, not the first DENY: the hard refusal is for spends ABOVE it.
Above the per-transaction cap, no signature is offered — a DENY, and the code names why.
